page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384gb is a memory-optimized server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB network-attached volume, and there are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and software compilation via Clang. Memory bandwidth performance is also exceptional, with uncached large-block read and write speeds ranking in the top 10%. Multi-threaded operations, such as Bzip3 decompression and Passmark CPU physics tests, fall within the top 25% tier. However, Passmark memory scores and large-model LLM inference prompt processing with a 70B model perform at an average level.

The server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads due to its dedicated AMD EPYC processor allocation and dense 384.0 GB RAM configuration. A key tradeoff is the lack of substantial local storage, as the instance relies on a 1 GB network-attached volume, which limits workloads requiring high-speed local NVMe scratch space. Additionally, the absence of a GPU makes it unsuitable for heavy parallel graphics or large-scale AI training. It is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, software compilation, text and image processing, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
